name: Intan
description: A star 48 parsecs away, 77% of the Sun's width, measured from its light.

radius.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 15578: radius 0.771 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 0.267 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.054) and temperature

temperature.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 15578: effective temperature 4729 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.04)

distance.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 15578: distance 48.189 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.012), at which the luminosity and radius hold

limb.none: no mass is measured and no spectroscopic surface gravity is published with this radius: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770 assume the gravity of their fit (table column 15)

text.card: A star 48 parsecs away, 77% of the Sun's width, measured from its light.
text.introduction: Its brightness, measured band by band, gives 0.267 times the Sun's luminosity at 4,729 K, so 0.771 solar radii.
text.locator: Table 2, HIP 15578: D, Teff, L, Rad, Q

quotes.title: HD 20868
quotes.card: HD 20868 is a star in the southern constellation Fornax.
quotes.introduction: With an apparent visual magnitude of 9.92, it is much too dim to be visible to the naked eye.
